items.title: Actual clipped-output exponential mean-error bounds

source.anchor: Appendix D.1 Claim2/Eq18 and Lemma B.12; consumed by SPHMC Appendix A.4(2)
source.attribution: ASTIS mathematical restatement and exposition of the clipping moment argument used by Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang, Smoothed Picard Hamiltonian Monte Carlo.

items.statement: m, mB and V are measurable. For every x, V(x)>=0 and abs(m(x)-mB(x))<=V(x). The function J(x)=exp(2*ell*V(x))-1 is integrable under q and qhat, with respective integrals at most 2*exp(-K) and 2*exp(2*B-K). The function exp(2*ell*abs(m(x)-mB(x)))-1 is qhat-integrable and its integral is at most 2*exp(2*B-K).
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, d=finrank(E)>0. The actual potential f is differentiable everywhere and its actual gradient is globally beta-Lipschitz. eta,beta,B>0 and ell>=2.
Set g=grad f(x_plus), h=x0-eta*g. Assume norm(h-x_plus)<=sqrt(d*eta) and 64*beta^2*(ell*d/B+ell^2)<=1/eta^2. These residual and step assumptions are retained exactly.

Let P=(z->sqrt(eta) z)_*stdGaussian(E), U=volume restricted to (0,1], nu=U product P and q=(z->h+sqrt(eta) z)_*stdGaussian(E). For s=(r,z), theta=pi*r/2, gamma=h+sin(theta)(x-h)+cos(theta)z and v=(pi/2)(cos(theta)(x-h)-sin(theta)z), define W(x,s)=<v,g-grad f(gamma)>.

Define m(x)=integral W(x,s) dnu(s), mB(x)=integral min(B,max(-B,W(x,s))) dnu(s), V(x)=integral max(abs(W(x,s))-B,0) dnu(s), qhat=q.tilted(mB), and K=min(B^2/(40*beta^2*d*eta^2),B/(8*beta*eta)). All functions and measures are actual definitions, not abstract witnesses.

formulae.label: Actual clipped-output moment
formulae.tex: \mathbb E_q[e^{2\ell V}-1]\le 2e^{-K},\qquad \mathbb E_{\widehat q}[e^{2\ell V}-1]\le 2e^{2B-K},\qquad \mathbb E_{\widehat q}[e^{2\ell|m-m_B|}-1]\le 2e^{2B-K}.

obligations.label: Actual proposal and clipped-output exponential mean-error integrability and bounds

bindings.boundary: This proves three exponential-minus-one integrability statements and their explicit bounds under the actual proposal and actual clipped tilt. ClippedGradientProgram already identifies qhat with the actual program output; this theorem does not repeat its pushforward equality. It does not assert normalized Radon-Nikodym power identities, a Renyi divergence bound, an ideal-target equality, a joint adaptive kernel, initialization or query cost. The factor 2 is retained and no logarithmic estimate is claimed. Neither full companion paper is complete.

assumption_deltas.source: Euclidean smooth sampling in positive dimension.
assumption_deltas.lean: Finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space with strictly positive finrank.
assumption_deltas.reason: Coordinate-free Gaussian and gradient interfaces retain the positive dimension assumption.

assumption_deltas.source: Positive smoothness, clipping and step parameters with Claim2 residual and step conditions.
assumption_deltas.lean: eta,beta,B,d>0,ell>=2, residual bound and the displayed 64-condition are retained.
assumption_deltas.reason: This packet does not extend to beta=0 or zero dimension.

assumption_deltas.lean: Restricted volume on (0,1], independently multiplied with the actual Gaussian.
assumption_deltas.reason: Endpoint differences have zero Lebesgue mass.

assumption_deltas.source: Appendix D.1 Claim2 and Eq18 use exponential clipping control under the implemented clipped law.
assumption_deltas.lean: Three explicit L1 statements and nonlogarithmic moment bounds, retaining factor 2 and constants 40 and 8.
assumption_deltas.reason: This is the moment dependency, not the entire normalized Renyi claim; no earlier logarithmic simplification is reused.

assumption_deltas.source: Conditional Jensen and changes of integration order are used in the moment argument.
assumption_deltas.lean: Joint L1 precedes Fubini; exponential section L1 is obtained q-almost everywhere; the actual mean-error bound is pointwise for every x.
assumption_deltas.reason: These distinct integrability and quantifier obligations are proved.
